'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Yemeni civil war (2014–present)|Yemeni Civil War]]
**Six [[Houthis]] and five [[Military of Yemen|Yemeni soldiers]] are killed during clashes in government-controlled [[Lahj Governorate]], [[Yemen]]. [https://english.news.cn/20230328/32a99a9f3e87447faa3305be4ee047b6/c.html (Xinhua)]
*[[Fazil Mustafa]], an opposition member of [[Azerbaijan]]'s [[National Assembly (Azerbaijan)|National Assembly]], is shot multiple times outside his home in [[Baku]] by unknown assailants in an [[assassination|assassination attempt]]. Mustafa's condition is described as satisfactory, and his life is not reported to be in danger. [https://news.az/news/azerbaijani-mp-fazil-mustafa-shot-near-his-home (News.az)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Ciudad Juárez migrant center fire]]
**[[Central America|Central]] and [[South America]]n [[immigration detention|detainees]] at a migrant center in [[Ciudad Juárez]], [[Chihuahua (state)|Chihuahua]], [[Mexico]], [[arson|deliberately set fire to]] their [[mattress]]es, killing 38 people and injuring 28 others. [https://apnews.com/article/mexico-fire-migrant-facility-dead-eea0b6efafd77f9868ef27ed1cf572b3 (AP)]
*Three people are killed, thirteen others are missing and 14 are rescued after a boat carrying [[Cameroon]]ian migrants [[capsize]]s near [[Saint Kitts]], [[Saint Kitts and Nevis]]. [https://apnews.com/article/antigua-boat-capsized-missing-dead-3a4393548ee5ad91a44d9687ec96a4d7 (AP)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2023 Lisbon Ismaili Centre stabbing]]
**Two Portuguese women are killed in a [[Stabbing as a terrorist tactic|stabbing attack]] at an [[Isma'ilism]] [[Shia Islam|Shia]] religious centre in [[Lisbon]], [[Portugal]]. [[Polícia de Segurança Pública|Police]] shoot the suspect, an Afghan man, in the leg at the scene, before arresting him and taking him to a hospital. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-65097098 (BBC News)]
*[[Killing of Hae Min Lee]]
**Adnan Syed's [[murder in United States law|murder]] [[conviction]] is reinstated by [[Maryland]]'s [[appeal court]], less than six months after [[Baltimore]] [[prosecutor]]s presented new evidence in the 1999 fatal strangulation of Hae Min Lee. [https://www.reuters.com/world/us/maryland-appeals-court-reinstates-murder-conviction-serial-podcast-subject-syed-2023-03-28/ (Reuters)]
*[[Clive Palmer]] sues [[Australia]] for AUD$296 billion over an iron ore project, over which his company, Mineralogy, had previously lost a [[Mineralogy v Western Australia|lawsuit]]. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2023-03-30/clive-palmer-to-sue-australia-for-300b-over-iron-ore-project/102166246 (ABC News)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Philippine drug war]]
**[[President of the Philippines|President]] [[Bongbong Marcos]] announces that the country will suspend relations with the [[International Criminal Court]] (ICC) due to the ICC's refusal to suspend its investigation of alleged crimes committed by the administration of former president [[Rodrigo Duterte]] during the country's [[Philippine drug war|war on drugs]]. [https://www.bnnbloomberg.ca/philippines-to-cut-contact-with-international-criminal-court-1.1901291 (Bloomberg)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2023 Scottish National Party leadership election]]
**The [[Scottish Parliament]] votes to elect [[Scottish National Party]] leader [[Humza Yousaf]] as [[First Minister of Scotland]], becoming the first [[person of color|non-white]] and first [[Islam in Scotland|Muslim]] to hold the position since it was created in 1999. [https://news.stv.tv/scotland/humza-yousaf-becomes-scotlands-sixth-first-minister-after-majority-vote-at-scottish-parliament (STV)]
*The [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour Party]]'s [[National Executive Committee of the Labour Party|National Executive Committee]] votes 22–12 to prevent former [[Leader of the Labour Party (UK)|leader]] [[Jeremy Corbyn]] from running as a candidate in their next election. [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-politics-65102128.amp (BBC)]
